newsitem.title: UK: Wolseley trims gains as broad market climbs.
newsitem.headline: Wolseley trims gains as broad market climbs.

text.p: Shares in Wolseley trimmed earlier on Wednesday despite the broad market tracking Wall Street higher.
By 1440, shares in the UK building materials group were up 8-1/2p to 472p, after having climbed to a nine week high earlier.
The initial rally was sparked by comments from the company, forecasting strength in its U.S. operations this year.
Merrill Lynch said yesterday it upgraded the shares to "accumulate" from "neutral."

Concerns that the strength in sterling would reduce profits pressured the shares last month, dealers said. Natwest was the latest brokerage to shave its profit estimates, reducing 1997 earnings by two percent, they said.
But dealers and analysts said Wolseley executives expressed optimism about the U.S. market.

ABN AMRO Hoare Govett analyst Donald Anderson met with Wolseley executives recently. Anderson, who has the shares among his top picks for 1997, said the Wolseley "seemed reasonably happy with the course of trade in their biggest market. There's no sign that the U.S. market will weaken in '97."
